newsitem.title: UGANDA: Ugandan army says two rebels killed in the north.
newsitem.headline: Ugandan army says two rebels killed in the north.

text.p: The Ugandan army on Thursday reported "skirmishes" in northwestern Uganda in which it killed two rebels of the West Nile Bank Front (WNBF) group.
A spokesman said the army and the rebels were involved in skirmishes along the border with Zaire, near the Ugandan town of Arua.
The spokesman made no mention of army casualties.
Aid workers spoke of reports of shelling near Arua but the army denied the conflict was at such levels.
On Tuesday, Ugandan President Yoweri Museveni said the army killed 230 "invaders" in the southwest, along the Zaire border.

Although the army and government have in the past blamed Zairean troops and Zairean-based Ugandan dissidents for attacks, Museveni on Tuesday blamed Sudan, specifically Moslem leader Hassan al-Tourabi.

Museveni has fought a number of rebel groups since he won a five-year bush war in 1986. The biggest such group now is the radical Christian Lord's Resistance Army, which wants to govern Uganda along the tenets of the biblical Ten Commandments.
Museveni's victory in presidential elections in May has not calmed rebel activity, which has occurred mainly in the north of the country.
